name: go-ansible-bounded-execution-output-with-3fcf
instr:
go-ansible cannot currently bound streamed Ansible output by bytes, records, or both across direct executions and workflows. Add shared, concurrency-safe accounting for complete committed output units. Preserve existing behavior when either allowance is zero.

The `outputlimit` package at `github.com/apenella/go-ansible/v2/pkg/execute/outputlimit` provides `OutputLimit`, `OutputUsage`, `ErrOutputLimit`, `OutputLimitError`, `NewOutputController`, and `OutputController`. Reject whole units before either allowance is crossed. Support `errors.Is` and expose final usage through `OutputLimitError.Usage`. Snapshots include only complete committed units, including when concurrent streams publish differently sized units.

`DefaultResults` from `defaultresult.NewDefaultResults` counts transformed lines and published bytes. `JSONStdoutCallbackResults` and `JSONLEventStdoutCallbackResults` from `jsonresults.NewJSONStdoutCallbackResults` and `jsonresults.NewJSONLEventStdoutCallbackResults` respectively count published JSON lines and valid emitted events. Suppressed timer messages and malformed JSONL consume nothing. Existing validation failures remain observable. Cancellation and destination failures stop accounting, preserve committed usage, and remain distinct from exhaustion.

`DefaultExecute` from `execute.NewDefaultExecute` shares one allowance across stdout and stderr. Return `ErrOutputLimit` only after exhaustion blocks another unit on either stream and the child exits, even if it
